_comment: Mutation arms whose mutation IS applied and whose named assertion does not see it, with
the reason, the SUBJECT that would see it, and who can produce that subject.
THIS FILE FAILS IN BOTH DIRECTIONS, like `ledger.json` beside it and
`ci/test/ci-coverage.known-dark.txt` one directory over. A registered arm that SURVIVES is
reported, counted, and does not fail the run. A registered arm that is KILLED fails the run
by name, demanding the entry be deleted — so an entry cannot outlive the gap it records, and
nobody has to remember to clean up after closing one.
ONLY A SURVIVAL IS EXCUSED. A registered arm that reports NEVER RAN still fails, and that is
the whole difference between this register and an exemption list. An entry says: this
mutation reaches the artefact, the assertion named below is green with the defect in place,
and here is the subject that would make it red. It does not say the arm may be broken — a
`find` that stopped matching, an assertion that was renamed, a tree that did not come back
are all still failures under an entry, because none of them is the claim the entry makes.
AN ENTRY IS ONLY LEGITIMATE WITH ALL SIX FIELDS, and `selftest.mjs` refuses the register
otherwise rather than reading around a missing one:
reason    — what the arm asserts and what is green with the mutation in place
cause     — WHY it survives, from readings and not from inference
subject   — the subject that would kill it, concretely enough to go and build
closed_by — who can produce that subject, and where the work lives
evidence  — what was measured, when, and on what tree
recorded  — the date this entry was written, so the debt is dated and not merely present
NOT LEGITIMATE, and the reason the bar is written down while this file is one entry long:
an arm that survives because the ASSERTION is weak does not belong here — strengthen the
assertion. An arm that survives because its mutated reading was taken from a session that
never came up does not belong here either — that is an instrument that did not run, and it
is reported as a stall, not as a survival. Both of those were live questions on the day this
file was written (`O/the-export-answers-for-the-live-path` was the first, fixed by making
the assertion per-region; `O2/a-control-on-every-row` is the second, still open), and both
were kept OUT of this file on purpose. A register whose bar is set once it is already long
gets the bar its longest-serving entries deserve.
COUNT THE KEYS IN `known_survivors`; do not trust a sentence here saying how many there are.
`ledger.json` records that its own summary line has been wrong four times, which is the one
error a register cannot afford, so this file does not carry that sentence at all.

P4/no-frame-is-current-on-a-live-session.reason: The arm removes `session_view.selectionDetail`'s position fallback — the loop that picks a frame by comparing `f.step` against `v.controls.step` when nothing has been marked `current` — and its named assertion, "LIVE: exactly one frame is current on arrival, before anything is clicked", stays GREEN. The mutation is applied, reaches the hydration bundle, and changes nothing observable on any surface a journey can drive.
P4/no-frame-is-current-on-a-live-session.cause: THREE WRITERS MARK A FRAME BEFORE `selectionDetail` EVER CONSULTS THE FALLBACK, and that was established by three readings rather than argued. (1) `selectCalltraceFrame` writes `CalltraceVM.selectedEntry` on a row click — the arm survived the post-click assertion at `clicked="calculate_damage" panel="calculate_damage"`, because the click writes the selection itself. (2) `selectLandingFrame` writes it on the landing — so the arm survived a newly added ARRIVAL assertion too, which is the reading the fallback would have to be load-bearing for. (3) Behind that, the recovery ANCHOR: re-aiming the mutation at `selectLandingFrame`'s own position walk (`if lines.len == 0: return false` forced true, so the walk never runs) ALSO survived, at "counted 1, the claim says 1", because `selectLandingFrame` tries `s.selectCalltraceFrame(anchor)` first and returns before the walk. With any of the three having marked a frame, `selectionDetail`'s first loop always sets `chosen` and the branch beneath it is unreachable.
P4/no-frame-is-current-on-a-live-session.subject: A LIVE session with NO recovery anchor whose `visibleLines` are empty at seed time. That is the one state in which all three writers decline and `selectionDetail` reaches the fallback: no anchor for `selectLandingFrame` to resolve, nothing for its position walk to walk, and no click yet. The corpus the journeys drive has no such recording — every subject either carries an anchor or seeds visible lines — so the arm's assertion is correct and simply has nothing to be correct ABOUT. Killing this arm needs that subject, not a stronger assertion.
P4/no-frame-is-current-on-a-live-session.closed_by: Whoever adds such a recording to the corpus the journeys drive, in THIS repository — `tools/journeys/lib/corpus.mjs` selects subjects from the served markup, so the work is a published recording that seeds no anchor and no visible lines, plus the subject filter that selects it. Then re-run `node tools/journeys/selftest.mjs --arm P4/` and delete this entry; the run will demand the deletion by name.
P4/no-frame-is-current-on-a-live-session.evidence: Measured 2026-09-28 in worktree `blocktracer-ci-green-env`, branched from `origin/dev`, over `client/dist` built by `just export-hydrated` against the three pinned sibling trees (codetracer af70456c, isonim 03f83497, nim-everywhere b2ce1c6b). CI run 35389764236 on ef24db5, `journeys-bite (5)`: SURVIVED in 65s, the only non-killed arm in that shard, and the arm's `why` records the same verdict from its author's own earlier readings. The 65s is itself part of the evidence — this is a survival from a session that came up, not from one that stalled.

R/the-landing-position-is-never-asked-ab.reason: The arm removes `hydrate.nim`'s `h.session.requestLandingLocals()` and the Values pane still fills at every landing. Its named assertion — "at least one session paints Values rows at the position it landed on, before any motion" — stays GREEN at COUNTED 4 of 4 sessions, not at one straggler. The mutation is applied and reaches the hydration bundle; nothing a journey can drive is different without that call.
R/the-landing-position-is-never-asked-ab.cause: THE CALL WAS WRITTEN FOR A STATE THE `lang` FIX REMOVED, and that is the honest limit of what has been established here. Its own comment records the incident it exists for, measured against the deployed dev channel: "`ct/load-locals` requests reaching the engine at landing, ZERO; Values rows, ZERO; the pane reading 'Reading the values at this position…' for as long as the tab was open." At that time the engine refused every `ct/load-locals` outright — it reads `lang` as a `Lang::wire_name` string and the pinned store sends an ordinal — so a landing with no values was indistinguishable from a landing whose request was deduplicated away, which is the mechanism the comment blames. With the translation in place the ordinary `StateVM` auto-load effect answers, and all four landings fill without this call. WHAT IS NOT ESTABLISHED: whether the dedup race the comment describes still exists and is simply not reachable on these four subjects, or whether it was only ever the refusal wearing its clothes. Removing the call is NOT sanctioned by this entry.
R/the-landing-position-is-never-asked-ab.subject: A live session on which `StateVM`'s auto-load effect is deduplicated away at the landing — the state the comment describes: a `requestLocals` issued before `startWorker`, never delivered and never completed, so the tracker holds the key and the served frame's position write finds its own arguments already pending and skips the send. None of the four sessions the journeys drive reaches it today. Producing one means controlling the order of worker startup against the first position write, which is hydration's own sequencing and not something the corpus can supply.
R/the-landing-position-is-never-asked-ab.closed_by: Whoever can drive hydration with that ordering — a harness hook that delays `startWorker` past the served frame's position write would do it, in THIS repository. Then re-run `node tools/journeys/selftest.mjs --arm R/the-landing-position-is-never-asked-about` and delete this entry: a registered arm that is KILLED fails the run by name.
R/the-landing-position-is-never-asked-ab.evidence: Measured 2026-10-16 in worktree `bt-ccp7` on `ccp7/writer-emits-compact`, over `client/dist` built by `just export-hydrated` against the three pinned sibling trees (codetracer af70456c, isonim 03f83497, nim-everywhere b2ce1c6b). CI run 38918156174, `journeys-bite (8)`: SURVIVED against its previous target, the equality "the Values pane at the landing position says what it says on returning to it" — which CANNOT see this defect by construction, since the mutation empties both sides and two empty sets compare equal. Re-aimed at the non-vacuity control and run locally: `SURVIVED — counted 4, the claim needs at least 1`, mutation restored, rendered hash b09f7b8bb948710a unchanged before and after.

PH2/a-session-at-tick-zero-has-no-positi.reason: The arm restores `positioned = step > 0` in `projectControls` — the sentinel the product retired — and the named assertion, "HYDRATED: the playhead is on the tick the session's own step names", stays GREEN. The mutation is applied and reaches the hydration bundle; the playhead is still drawn on the right tick.
PH2/a-session-at-tick-zero-has-no-positi.cause: BOTH ARMS READ AFTER THE ENGINE'S FIRST REPORT, AND BY THEN THE STEP IS NOT ZERO. `step > 0` is false only while the step IS zero, which is the window between hydration starting and the engine answering with a position — the state the arm's own `why` describes, "a session the engine has PARKED on the first step and a session that has heard nothing hold the same number". Both `hydratedArm` calls settle on the session reaching `ready`, which is after that answer. Re-aiming at `HYDRATED-REAL`, the chain capture whose SERVED frame stands at step 0 of 790, was tried and survives for the same reason: measured, `step 1 of 790 names tick 1 of 48 — drew 48 ticks, playhead on 1 (1 marked)`. The served frame's own playhead is drawn by the exporter and is not routed through `projectControls` at all, so the pre-hydration reading cannot see the mutation either.
PH2/a-session-at-tick-zero-has-no-positi.subject: A reading taken while the session is LIVE and the engine has not yet reported a position — `phase` past `fetching`, `controls` driven by `projectControls`, and `rrTicks` still at the `ReplayDataStore` initial 0. None of the journeys can take that reading today: they settle on `ready`, which is defined as the engine having answered. Producing it means a settle predicate that stops at the live-but-unanswered state and holds the session there long enough to read the timeline.
PH2/a-session-at-tick-zero-has-no-positi.closed_by: Whoever adds that settle state to `probe.mjs`'s `visit` — a predicate that admits `live && !engineReported` and a hold that keeps it there — in THIS repository. Then re-run `node tools/journeys/selftest.mjs --arm PH2/a-session-at-tick-zero-has-no-position-again` and delete this entry: a registered arm that is KILLED fails the run by name.
PH2/a-session-at-tick-zero-has-no-positi.evidence: Measured 2026-10-16 in worktree `bt-ccp7` on `ccp7/writer-emits-compact`, over `client/dist` built by `just export-hydrated` against the three pinned sibling trees (codetracer af70456c, isonim 03f83497, nim-everywhere b2ce1c6b). CI run 38918156174, `journeys-bite (8)`: SURVIVED on the `HYDRATED` arm. Re-aimed at `HYDRATED-REAL` and run locally: SURVIVED, with the reading above. Mutation restored both times; rendered hash b09f7b8bb948710a unchanged before and after.

N/the-position-is-compared-by-number-alo.reason: The arm removes the `|| after.markedDoc !== before.markedDoc` term from `positionMoved` in `09-a-jump-moves-the-position.journey.mjs`, leaving the comparison an integer one, and its named assertion "the marked position moved to the row's step" stays GREEN. The mutation is applied and reaches the instrument (its hash moves, fc1be0035c8b97cd -> 3dc66a50ed453abe); the verdict does not.
N/the-position-is-compared-by-number-alo.cause: THE ARM'S PREMISE IS ABOUT A SUBJECT THAT IS NO LONGER THERE, and the harness printed the replacement rather than leaving it to be inferred: `D-src-main-nr:13 -> D-src-main-nr:1`. The arm's `why` says "jumping there moves the mark from `main.nr:1` to `shield.nr:1` — the number is 1 both times and the FILE is not", which is what makes the document term load-bearing. The jump this journey actually exercises today stays inside ONE document and changes the number, so the integer comparison alone separates before from after and deleting the document term costs nothing. Nothing about the journey or the product weakened: the corpus moved under the arm, on the day the live call trace landed, which the arm's own last sentence anticipated for the demo arm without noticing it applied to this reading too.
N/the-position-is-compared-by-number-alo.subject: A session whose first row naming a step it is not on jumps to a DIFFERENT document at the SAME line number — `a.nr:7` -> `b.nr:7`. That is the only shape in which an integer comparison reads a working jump as a mark that never moved, which is the direction the arm exists to forbid. With such a row in the corpus this mutation turns the assertion red on the spot.
N/the-position-is-compared-by-number-alo.closed_by: Whoever curates the corpus the journeys drive, in THIS repository. `tools/journeys/lib/corpus.mjs` selects subjects out of the served markup, so the work is a published recording with two documents whose call-trace rows land on the same line number in each, plus the subject filter that picks it. Then re-run `node tools/journeys/selftest.mjs --arm N/the-position-is-compared` and delete this entry; the run will demand the deletion by name.
N/the-position-is-compared-by-number-alo.evidence: Measured 2026-10-22 in worktree `bt-ccp7` at f6a5e2a, over `client/dist` built by `just export-hydrated` against the three pinned sibling trees (codetracer af70456c, isonim 03f83497, nim-everywhere b2ce1c6b). `node tools/journeys/selftest.mjs --arm N/the-position-is-compared-by-number-alone`: before GREEN, mutated SURVIVED in 40s reporting `D-src-main-nr:13 -> D-src-main-nr:1`, after GREEN again. The same arm SURVIVED in CI run 39400689697, `journeys-bite (6)`.

O1/the-engine-never-gets-the-source.reason: The arm replaces `let files = sourceFilesOf(island)` in `client/hydrate/live_source.nim` with an empty seq, so the recording's own source never reaches the engine's VFS, and its named assertion "a value's origin is actually CLASSIFIED, not merely answered" stays GREEN at `counted 2, the claim needs at least 1`. The mutation reaches the artefact — rendered 8ac3f88d8b9c7fb8 -> 64a3c791b6a95cbf, 1967560 -> 1964273 bytes — so this is not an arm that failed to apply.
O1/the-engine-never-gets-the-source.cause: THE COUNT IS 2 WITH THE SOURCE AND 2 WITHOUT IT, so the assertion is not blind to the defect by being weak at the margin — it is measuring two hops that do not depend on the recording's source reaching the VFS at all. The assertion that DOES move is the journey's next one, "no hop reports 'source unavailable' on a recording that published source", and re-aiming the arm there was TRIED on 2026-10-22 and is not available: it reports NEVER RAN — ALREADY RED, `4 of 6 did`. That is the red `ledger.json` carries for `a-value-can-be-traced-to-its-origin`. So the arm is pointed at the only assertion in that journey which is both green and reachable, and that assertion's subject cannot exhibit the defect.
O1/the-engine-never-gets-the-source.subject: A recording whose published source attributes all six hops, so `unavailable == 0` and the journey's third assertion is GREEN on the unmutated tree. This is the same work `ledger.json`'s `a-value-can-be-traced-to-its-origin` entry already tracks — not a second thing to build. The moment that ledger entry closes, re-aim this arm at "no hop reports 'source unavailable'" and this exact mutation kills it: with no source in the VFS every hop says 'source unavailable', which is the arm's own `why` describing the state before the fix.
O1/the-engine-never-gets-the-source.closed_by: Whoever closes `ledger.json`'s `a-value-can-be-traced-to-its-origin` entry, in THIS repository — the two are one piece of work and this register should not imply otherwise. Then change this arm's `assertion` field to "no hop reports 'source unavailable' on a recording that published source", re-run `node tools/journeys/selftest.mjs --arm O1/the-engine-never-gets-the-source`, and delete this entry; the run will demand the deletion by name.
O1/the-engine-never-gets-the-source.evidence: Measured 2026-10-22 in worktree `bt-ccp7` at f6a5e2a, over `client/dist` built by `just export-hydrated` against the three pinned sibling trees (codetracer af70456c, isonim 03f83497, nim-everywhere b2ce1c6b). Arm as written: SURVIVED in 142s, `counted 2, the claim needs at least 1`. Arm re-aimed at the third assertion: NEVER RAN — ALREADY RED, `4 of 6 did; 0 said 'unparseable source line'`, in 43s; the re-aim was then reverted. The arm SURVIVED in CI run 39400689697, `journeys-bite (3)`.
